prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied B rhythm-game frame.
Change ONLY the four movable button caps into visibly sculpted MECHANICAL KEYBOARD KEYCAPS. The user wants the actual keycap shape to look different from the present flat metal slabs. Keep the EXACT existing camera angle, portrait composition, four-key positions, spacing and broad rhythm-game striking area. Do not choose a new viewpoint to show the caps.

Design large blank sculpted keyboard keycaps: gently dished concave square tops, generously rounded square corners, smooth shoulders, and substantial curved/sloping front and side skirts that flare toward the bottom. Make the keycap shape and front skirt readable from THIS existing view through shading and a clear dark separation gap above its socket. Use tactile satin dark-charcoal keycap material, with a soft highlight following the dished lip; remove the old bright silver picture-frame rim around each cap. They should unmistakably look like oversized physical keyboard keycaps, not flat panels, touch screens, rectangular metal blocks or round arcade buttons. Let the height follow naturally from that shape; do not exaggerate height or enforce a numeric height increase.

Retain the depicted state: keys 1, 3 and 4 are raised dark neutral keycaps; ONLY key 2 from the left is visibly pressed down and lit pale cyan across its SCULPTED CONCAVE top, with its shape still readable. Preserve the white-centered cyan flash in the single wide aperture directly below key 2. Keep all four lower support housings and their existing single open apertures unchanged. Keep the flash compact and facing the viewer.
Everything outside the movable keycaps stays unchanged: fixed sockets, four emitter openings, bottom bumper, full silver/navy/gold armor, tall cyan side gauges without ticks, dark lane field, background, composition, scale and perspective. No text or key legends, letters, symbols, logos, extra controls, panels or cropping. Make this a clear keycap redesign, not another edge-polish pass.
